source: SMTD Course Descriptions Index Google Docs (linked from smtd.umich.edu Students > Course Descriptions)

courses.title: Performing Arts Management
courses.description: An introduction and overview of management issues concerning the non-profit cultural sector. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Your Career in the Arts
courses.description: To forge a viable performing arts career, young professionals need a compass - a flexible tool for goal-setting and making strategic decisions. In this course, students develop basic visioning and business strategy skills to create an individualized plan for their arts career through the business model canvas. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Money Smarts for Artists
courses.description: Artists often treat "money" as a dirty word, yet difficulty managing finances is one of the primary reasons arts professionals leave the field. This course explores questions surrounding individual arts economics, from budgeting to balancing multiple income streams. Students will develop personal financial strategy as a capstone project. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: This course provides access to the greatest leaders from the fields of performing arts, arts administration, arts leadership and philanthropy. Students have the opportunity for multi-faceted in-depth engagement and reflection with different arts leaders every week through a Guest Leader Interview and Leader Reading. The premise of the class is to ignite learning through inspiration from and role modeling by successful leaders and direct mentorship. Students engage with each leader in a virtual forum through interactive video lectures, comprehensive leadership readings and facilitated group discussions and synthesis of learned leadership best practices. Following each guest leader session, reading and discussion, students write and submit reflection papers. As the final project, students will present a mini-lecture online, engage in a peer Q and A and provide critical feedback. In addition, students participate in an on-site practicum, where they have the opportunity to shadow, interview and observe a leader first-hand. Class sessions are conducted virtually through an online lecture platform. Typically offered Fall, Winter depending on available content

courses.title: Arts Entrepreneurship Forum
courses.description: This seminar series invites provocative, pioneering, influential, and accomplished musicians, actors, dancers, arts entrepreneurs, and leaders to speak with students about their personal experiences developing, financing, and managing their artistic practice, projects, and ventures. Participants will learn about artistic curation, production, fundraising, marketing, management, fan development, audience experience, intellectual property, mentoring, and career survival skills, among other topics keyed to the visitor's expertise. Following a lecture and discussion, students will be able to meet the guest speaker and network with members of the arts entrepreneurial community. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Leading and Managing U.S. Global Majority Cultural Organizations
courses.description: Leading and Managing Global Majority Cultural Organizations educates students about the impacts of racism in U.S. society on global majority cultural organizations. The course also uses service learning with a global majority cultural organization to deeply engage students in the deliberate practice of learning to lead and manage. Fulfills the Race and Ethnicity requirement for SMTD majors only; dual degree students should take an approved course under LSA.

courses.title: DIY Marketing and Social Media
courses.description: The internet presents an array of low cost tools individuals can use to share and promote their career. This course addresses marketing theory the beast practices that allow individuals to create a professional social marketing toolkit. Offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Writing About Your Art; Bios, Blogs, and Websites
courses.description: Artists must be advocates for their creative vision. Writing well about your art can help identify your creative voice and inspire others to support your work. In this course, students will explore how to write about their art through blogs, websites, program notes, and social media, culminating in an advocacy plan targeting their goals. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Grant Writing and Fundraising Basics
courses.description: Fundraising is critical in the arts and even individual artists have many avenues available to raise money. This course covers how to argue the importance of artistic work, budgeting, and writing successful proposals. Students will be exposed to grant, donation, and crowd-funding opportunities, and will complete a fundraising plan for a project. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Legal Essentials for Artists
courses.description: This course addresses foundational legal principles and practice-based skills that will help musicians, dancers, and actors identify legal issues, negotiate contracts, and integrate legal strategies into their career objectives. Topics will include: copyright, intellectual property rights, royalties, and contract law, among others. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Fundraising and the Arts
courses.description: A review and analysis of philanthropy and development in America's cultural life and the role of both the public and private sectors. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Arts Leadership
courses.description: This course explores the theory and practice of leadership in the non- and for-profit arts sector. Students will learn the history and structure of non-profits, especially board leadership and fiduciary oversight. They'll explore executive leadership, including strategic planning, budgeting, and organizational renewal. Course participants will actively engage with leaders in the field. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Running Your Own Ensemble, Theatre Troupe, or Dance Company
courses.description: Creating your own arts organization can provide a vibrant career path, but getting started can be daunting. This course give students the tools needed to jumpstart sustainable careers in music, theatre, and dance. Topics will include: your artistic identity, business models, branding and marketing, financial planning, legal pitfalls, and fundraising. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: The Recording Industry; Selling Your Music to the World
courses.description: Musicians face many questions when considering how to release the music they've created. This class focuses on the real-world application of the entrepreneurial, legal, business, and artistic considerations required to sell music today. Students will learn about the entire recording process, including bringing music to market, and current industry trends and future opportunities. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Media Technology Careers
courses.description: This course explores how today's leading technology companies bring products to market and how artists, musicians, composers, engineers, business and computer science students might contribute and become part of these companies. Topics include best practices to department functions. Online resources offer insights into real, working companies. Instructor will visit campus to meet with students. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Arts Entrepreneurship Essentials
courses.description: Arts Entrepreneurship Essentials is a comprehensive journey that begins with developing one’s mindset of conceiving, vetting and formulating an idea and then implementing them into successful, sustainable creative ventures. Students will have the opportunity to explore entrepreneurship through the prism of their own arts or life focus and specialization. Required texts, coupled with class lectures, projects and engaged discussions are designed to help develop the core skillsets necessary to awaken and develop young creative entrepreneurs. As a practicing arts and social entrepreneur having founded several successful, ongoing creative initiatives and organizations, Professor Dworkin will introduce a unique and practical course informed by his own life experiences, including building a 10 million dollar non-profit with track record over several decades. As an overall philosophy, this course demystifies entrepreneurship and illustrates how an authentic passion and commitment to creativity and learning serve as key pillars for a successful, fulfilling life. The final Capstone Project will tie together the material covered in all modules, showcasing each student’s ability to formulate and make the case for a creative venture. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Business of Music
courses.description: A survey of professional opportunities in performing arts management, the recording industry and arts entrepreneurship, with a focus on building business skills for the personal development of a career in music. Students will learn basic skills that may serve any of the Business of Music areas of concentration: leadership, planning, budgeting, financial analysis, marketing, fund-raising and development (and/or seeking investors). Assignments will include: analysis of case studies, writing a grant proposal, and working in teams to create a model arts enterprise that will need a business plan and marketing materials. The course also features a number of guests from various businesses and music disciplines. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Music Industry Workshop; Starting Music Businesses
courses.description: The music industry is undergoing enormous changes fueled by social and technological shifts. In this course, participants will work in teams to envision music-oriented businesses. Teams will assess opportunities, research customers, and formulate a business and marketing plan. Students will choose whether to continue their venture at the semester's end. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Creating Social Value through the Arts
courses.description: This course posits that the purpose of art making is to create a better society. Students will explore the social role of the arts historically and how arts organizations create value today. Teams will research a target audience, execute and arts experience, and measure the event's impact. Participants will refine skills in idea generation, public speaking, and data assessment to enhance social impact. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Performing Arts Internship
courses.description: Supervised internship in cooperation with a professional organization. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Special Projects
courses.description: Independent study for individual students or project teams. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall and Winter

courses.title: EXCELerator; Practicum
courses.description: This course provides a for-credit option for students involved in an entrepreneurship venture and intensive mentoring of the EXCELerator incubator fellowship and thus recognition of both the learning gained as well as the time and focus necessary to succeed in an EXCELerator project. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Community Service Project
courses.description: An independent study course for students interested in completing a social enterprise or community service project. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.description: This is the introductory level course in conducting. Emphasis is on baton technique, non-verbal communication, musical decision-making as a conductor, and developing an informed aural image. SMTD or advanced musically-trained students; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Elementary Conducting II
courses.description: This is the second introductory level course in conducting. Emphasis is on score study, building the informed aural image, baton technique, non-verbal communication, and leading small-scale rehearsals. Prerequisite: CONDUCT 315; SMTD or advanced musically-trained students; instructor permission; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Advanced Instrumental Conducting I

courses.title: Introduction to Dance
courses.description: Introductory studio dance courses provide instruction in technical and creative aspects of a variety of dance genres. Each section under this course listing is devoted to a different dance genre. Section/genres include: contemporary/modern dance; ballet; jazz; hip hop; and special topics such as dance improvisation. In each of these sections, principles of alignment, rhythmic and spatial awareness, dynamic, flexibility, and strength are investigated as foundations for freedom of expression. Very brief reading and writing assignments, as well as performance and video viewing and analysis, inform the work in the studio. Courses culminate in the sharing of technical accomplishments and creative work. Non-Dance majors only; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Modern Dance I
courses.description: An introduction to modern and contemporary dance techniques. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Modern Dance I
courses.description: Dance techniques from mid-20th century American modern dance, with focus on one or two particular styles of training. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Commercial Dance Styles I
courses.description: Dancers will gain a working knowledge of commercial and concert jazz dance styles as a practical performance model. Dancers will develop the skills necessary to learn technique at a professional level through open awareness of practiced movements and combinations while strengthening their performance aesthetic. Jazz dance is about style and discipline. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Dance I
courses.description: First-year studio course in principles of contemporary modern dance technique for dance majors, building upon principles of alignment, training, movement dynamics, rhythmic phrasing, and its potential for expression as an art form. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Humphrey I/II
courses.description: Dancers will gain a working knowledge of the Humphrey/Weidman technique as a practical body training practice, including history and movement philosophies. This course will cover beginner/intermediate technical practices in the Humphrey/Weidman tradition with a Limon influence. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Legacy Dance I/II
courses.description: This course will cover beginner/intermediate practices from one of the 20th century American modern dance legacies, such as Horton, Graham, Limon, Dunham, and Cunningham. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Ballet I
courses.description: An intermediate ballet course which focuses on the basic placement concepts of transfer of weight, core-strength, a solid standing leg, and the positions of the body. Proper alignment will be stressed in all of the exercises at the barre and in the centre. Centre work is designed to impart solid turning and jumping skills including en dehors and en dedans pirouettes, traveling turns, basic petit allegro and grand allegro vocabulary. Emphasis will be placed on musicality and transitions. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Ballet I
courses.description: An intermediate ballet course which focuses on the basic placement concepts or transfer of weight, core-strength, a solid standing leg, and the positions of the body. Proper alignment will be stressed in all of the exercises at the barre and in the centre. Centre work is designed to impart solid turning and jumping skills including en dehors and en dedans pirouettes, traveling turns, basic petite allegro and grand allegro vocabulary. Emphasis will be placed on musicality and transitions. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Ballet I
courses.description: Survey of principles of basic ballet placement, barre and center work to prepare for allegro, jumps and sequences across the floor. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Ballet I
courses.description: Survey of principles of basic ballet placement, barre and center work to prepare for allegro, jumps and sequences across the floor. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Ballet Fundamentals I
courses.description: This course is designed to give students a solid base in ballet technique and an understanding of the fundamental movement principles that underlie it. Students explore core concepts of technique, dynamic alignment and anatomically sound movement while developing coordination, rhythmic and spatial awareness, and artistic elements with a sense of performance. Department consent required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Ballet Fundamentals II
courses.description: This course builds upon the ballet skills, vocabulary and fundamental movement principles taught in Ballet Fundamentals 1. Students explore core concepts of technique, dynamic alignment, anatomically sound movement, rhythmic and spatial awareness through more complex movement phrases while continuing to learn new vocabulary and a sense of artistic expression and performance. Prerequisite: DANCE 115; Department consent required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: First Year Repertory
courses.description: Cast by audition, repertory groups rehearse works by faculty and guest choreographers for the annual production of the University Dance Company at the Power Center and other venues. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: First Year Repertory
courses.description: Cast by audition, repertory groups rehearse works by faculty and guest choreographers for the annual production of the University Dance Company at the Power Center and other venues. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: First-Year Dance Company
courses.description: In the model of a repertory dance company, students learn, rehearse, produce, and tour new and existing repertory works by faculty and guest choreographers for performances, master classes, and lecture demonstrations in various locations throughout the region. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: First-Year Dance Lab
courses.description: Course content to complement core technique classes in the curriculum. May include Pilates, Yoga, Partnering, Cross-Training, Congolese, in addition to Ballet and Modern Technique courses. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: First-Year Dance Lab
courses.description: Course content to complement core technique classes in the curriculum. May include Pilates, Yoga, Partnering, Cross-Training, Congolese, in addition to Ballet and Modern Technique courses. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Dance Composition 1
courses.description: Students are introduced to basic elements of the craft of choreography: space, time, force, and motivation; concepts that can be applied to any genre of dance. Topics will be approached through improvisation, movement studies, readings, performance and video viewing, and written assignments. Concepts will be explored both as soloists and in small groups, and will conclude in a final composition showing. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Dance Composition 2
courses.description: Study of dance forms and their relationship to the other arts, exploring motivations and source materials. Prerequisite: DANCE 131; Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Movement Composition for Dance Minors
courses.description: Dance minors are introduced to basic elements of the craft of choreography: space, time, force, and motivation. Topics will be approached through improvisation, movement studies, readings, performance and video viewing, and written assignments. Concepts will be explored both as soloists and in small groups, concluding in a final composition showing. Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Film and Field Production
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with a thorough understanding of the fundamentals of field and film production by employing the art of dance as a medium of conceptual storytelling. Through the use of pre-, production-, and post-production principles, students will gain knowledge and skills to support the aesthetics of individual cinematic expression. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology for Dancers
courses.description: This course will give an overview of the musculoskeletal anatomy and its association to movement, common dance injuries linked to specific anatomy, with interaction of physiological systems into whole body anatomy. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Kinesiology for Dancers: A Guide to Injury Prevention
courses.description: This course aims to inform students about fundamental cross-training, injury prevention, and self-care knowledge through the introduction of kinesiologic principles. Students will learn basic and intermediate principles of biomechanics, exercise physiology, and motor control. Prerequisite: Dance 153 with a grade of C or better; Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Introduction to the Fundamentals of Acting
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of Acting affords 1st year Dance students the opportunity to engage in performative inquiry that is essential to their development as professional dancers and dancemakers. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Pilates/Integrative Movement Introduction
courses.description: An introduction to the mind-body method of Pilates, students explore anatomy and functional movement patterns. This physical practice course provides context for the evolution of classical and contemporary Pilates, and incorporates supplemental exercises from Gyrokinesis, yoga, and functional strength training. Various props such as yoga blocks, tennis balls, and foam rollers offer proprioceptive feedback, stability challenges, and myofascial release. The course goal is to increase breath awareness, balance, movement efficiency, strength and stability. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: First-Year Seminar
courses.description: The First-Year Seminar will provide students with tools to make more informed choices about nutrition, injury prevention, balancing physical practice with academic requirements and will teach them how to navigate advanced studies in dance within the university. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall DANCE 200-299

courses.title: Floorwork Fundamentals
courses.description: This course is to develop the industrious technical baseline of our dancing and align it with our risk-taking and choice-making sensibilities. We will build upon the integrity and responsive nature of the feet with real-time challenges that open up and strengthen our ability to adapt to shifting forces/environments. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Dance II
courses.description: Dance techniques from mid-20th century American modern dance, with particular focus on placement, phrasing, and dynamics. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Commercial Dance Styles II
courses.description: Dancers will gain a working knowledge of commercial and concert jazz dance styles as a practical performance mode at the intermediate level. Dancers will develop the skills necessary to learn technique at a professional level through open awareness of practiced movements and combinations while strengthening their performance aesthetic. Jazz dance is about style and discipline. Prerequisite: DANCE 103 with a grade of B or better; Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Dance II
courses.description: Second-year studio course in principles of contemporary modern dance technique for dance majors, building upon principles of alignment, training, movement dynamics, rhythmic phrasing, and its potential for expression as an art form. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Partnering
courses.description: We begin by generating heat via contact based exercises, sustaining tensile strength while others push, pull, pivot, and slide. We will become builders of evolving architecture that is made possible through collaboration. We will continue to awaken our ability to read each other through sequences/prompts that traverse the space together in tandem. This training is simultaneously coupled with improvisational and awareness propositions that aim to awaken the senses and their direct relationship to moving with another body. These opportunities reach beyond the singular agency of choosing for oneself and extend it to the composite understanding of shared decision making, of choice/consequence; this brings dancers' natural empathic acumen to the community level. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Tai Chi Fusion
courses.description: Students will explore intermediate Contemporary dance blended with Tai Chi. This martial art based dance class will explore cultural and historical information as well as offer a robust physical practice using contemporary dance practices. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Ballet II
courses.description: An intermediate ballet course which focuses on placement concepts such as transfer of weight, core-strength, a solid standing leg, and the positions of the body. Proper alignment will be stressed in all of the exercises at the barre and in the centre. Centre work is designed to impart solid turning and jumping skills including en dehors and en dedans pirouettes, traveling turns, basic petit allegro and grand allegro vocabulary. Emphasis will be placed on more difficult combinations of movements. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Ballet II
courses.description: An intermediate ballet course which focuses on placement concepts such as transfer of weight, core-strength, a solid standing leg, and the positions of the body. Proper alignment will be stressed in all of the exercises at the barre and in the centre. Centre work is designed to impart solid turning and jumping skills including en dohors and en dedans pirouettes, traveling turns, basic petite allegro and grand allegro vocabulary. Emphasis will be placed on more difficult combination of movements. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Ballet II
courses.description: Sophomore-level, continuation of barre, center and sequences across the floor, stressing phrasing and range, from adagio to petit allegro. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Ballet II
courses.description: Continuation of barre, center and sequences across the floor, stressing phrasing and range, from adagio to petit allegro. Prerequisite: Completion of freshman technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.description: Cast by audition, repertory groups rehearse works by faculty and guest choreographers for the annual production of the University Dance Company at the Power Center and other venues. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Dance Composition 3
courses.description: Sophomore-level survey of uses of rhythm, design, dynamics and motivation, leading to the creation and performance of solo and group works with emphasis on the relationship of music to choreography. Prerequisite: DANCE 132. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Dance Composition 4
courses.description: This course examines a series of ways to map movement and sound with the goal of cultivating an awareness of how the impact of movement can be deepened and extended through the informed choice of sound / music/ silence. Other topics addressed include chance structures, aural backdrop, and collaboration between composer and choreographer. Prerequisite: DANCE 231. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: The Integration of Music and Movement
courses.description: In this course, dancers will learn the principles of meter and form through lessons in interactive kinesthetic engagement. Students will incorporate movement with musical exercises that will enable them to develop a solid, musical foundation, and will provide them with the skills required to construct, comprehend, and execute rhythmic and gestural combinations. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Dance Criticism and Media
courses.description: Explore the art of dance criticism through history, writing, and media. This course dives into the role and evolution of the critic, and the impact of media on dance, in the United States. Students will learn to articulate their thoughts on dance performance, technique, and aesthetics through engaging writing, video-making, and discussions. Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Dance and Society
courses.description: This course investigates diverse dance cultures in various cultural, historical, and social contexts as well as their global travel and relocation through the perspective of dance and transnationalism. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Technical Production
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to equip dance artists with technical theater knowledge and abilities, incorporating state production elements. The basics of sound, costumes, props, lighting and scenery are presented. Students learn how to work and communicate with technical designers and crew members. Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Congolese Dance 1
courses.description: Study of traditional dances of the African Congo. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Congolese Dance 1
courses.description: Study of traditional dances of the African Congo. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Afro-Caribbean Dance
courses.description: Study of the various folkloric dance forms of the Caribbean, particularly those of Cuba, Haiti, and Brazil. Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Progressing Ballet Technique: Conditioning/Strengthening
courses.description: Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is a body-conditioning and strengthening somatic class that has been designed to enhance students' ballet technique by focusing on core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body with a gradual approach of carefully designed exercises. Repetitions of these exercises trigger the muscle memory required for any and all forms of dance. Class will incorporate exercises from Progressing Contemporary Technique (PCT). Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Design Fundamentals for Dance
courses.description: This course introduces students to the fundamentals of lighting, projection, and sound design. Students will explore both creative and technical aspects, including industry software, while highlighting collaboration between choreographers and designers. They will develop skills to interpret and integrate these elements as essential parts of dance performance design. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Community Engaged Pedagogy
courses.description: CEP works in tandem with the University of Michigan Chapter of Ballet and Books (B&B) to provide free ballet classes and literacy support to marginalized kids in the Ann Arbor and Ypsilanti community. The semester is divided into two parts: classroom lectures/workshops and onsite programming. Lecture topics include techniques for teaching pre-ballet, teaching hybridized dance and literacy classes, and basics of early childhood education. Department consent required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Empowering the Performing Artist
courses.description: Take your performance and your life to the next level. This course helps you build confidence, boost resilience, avoid burnout, and manage stress so you can shine on stage and off. You?ll learn to work through imposter syndrome, push past resistance, get out of your own way, and balance ambition with self-care through hands-on exercises, taking creative risks, and learning strategies backed by research from psychology and sports science. Join a collaborative cohort, set goals, and gain practical tools to level up as a performer and as a human being! Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Dance III
courses.description: Dance techniques from mid-20th century American modern dance, integrating technical ability with choreographic intent. Prerequisite: Completion of sophomore technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Modern Dance III
courses.description: Dance techniques from mid-20th century American modern dance, integrating technical ability with choreographic intent. Prerequisite: Completion of sophomore technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Commercial Dance Styles III/IV
courses.description: Dancers will gain a working knowledge of commercial and concert jazz dance styles as a practical performance mode at the advanced level. Dancers will develop the skills necessary to learn technique at a professional level through open awareness of practiced movements and combinations while strengthening their performance aesthetic. Jazz dance is about style and discipline. Prerequisite: DANCE 103 and 203 with a grade of B or better. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Dance III
courses.description: Dance techniques from mid-20th century American modern dance, with a particular focus integrating technical ability with musicality, phrasing and performance projection. Prerequisite: Completion of sophomore technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Humphrey Level III/IV
courses.description: Advanced practice of the Humphrey dance technique. Practice will focus on deepening the understanding and embodiment of Fall, Recovery, Suspension, Breath and the use of the spiral through the spine. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Legacy Dance III/IV
courses.description: This course will cover advanced practices from one of the 20th century American modern dance legacies, same as Dance 106. Prerequisite: DANCE 105 or 106 with a grade of B or better. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Ballet III
courses.description: This course is a continuation of working on alignment and proper execution of technique that encompasses the following: advanced barre work, en de hors and en de dans pirouettes, find tuning execution of basic material, self-discovery and self-correction of mistakes, awareness of other dancers, discovering value of plie and brush in petit allegro, piecing together more complicated/advanced petite allegro, and the use of imagery to enhance the thought process and the physical execution. Prerequisite: Completion of sophomore technique. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.description: The focus of the class will be on pointe work, strengthening the dancer's technique, proper alignment, core strength, precision in footwork, musicality, versatility/understanding of ballet styles. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Advanced Dance Making Lab
courses.description: Advanced Dance Making Lab will be offered in the second semester of the student's Junior year. Comprised of researching and engaging in intensive compositional practices, students will have an opportunity to focus on choreographing and directing group ensemble works. Students will attend to the ongoing, dailiness that is an essential requirement in the development and cultivation of a distinctive dance making practice, and to experience choreography as research. Prerequisite: Completion of Dance composition sequence: Dance 132 - 232. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Movement Improvisation
courses.description: The in-depth study and practice of improvisation as a performing art. Recognizing three strands of improvisational practice: bodily exploration, honing and cultivating aesthetic values and observational skill to compose dances in the moment will influence and shape process. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Performance Practices Through Collaboration
courses.description: This course will offer students the opportunity to create original performance through collaboration, working in a variety of media. Students from a variety of disciplines will engage in essential and highly interactive experiments to ask questions about what performance can be, and why it matters across a broad spectrum of topics. Students will gain awareness of what it means to create performances publicly and imaginatively. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Solo Performance
courses.description: This course will deepen students’ understanding and practice of making solo dances. Previous modalities may be explored in more detail and new modalities will be developed, culminating in a filmed version of the BFA capstone solo at the end of the semester. Prerequisites: Dance 131, 132, 231, 232 with a grade of C+ or better. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Topics in World Dance
courses.description: This course offers an opportunity to gain insight into the functions, aesthetics, history, and cultural context of dances within specific societies. Theatrical, religious, popular, and social dance traditions will be examined in widely varied cultures. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: History of American Modern Dance
courses.description: This course unpacks the history of American modern dance in the 20th and 21st centuries chronologically and introduces the cutting-edge discussions in Anglophone dance studies about this subject. We will conduct aesthetic and choreographic analysis to explore the embodiment of key concepts such as (post)modernism, individualism, freedom of expression, and abstraction that penetrated the concretization of American dance in the past over a hundred years. We will also examine how critical race theories and gender studies complement the historicization and theorization of modern dance. Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: History of the Black Ballerina
courses.description: This class examines the past and present experiences of Black-identifying dancers in ballet as well as the representation of people and cultures from the Black and African diasporas within the classical ballet narrative canon. We will give special attention to Black women in ballet and will also look at the movement towards creating space and opportunities for gender non-binary ballet dancers. We will look at ballet's racial and sociopolitical issues as they pertain to national and international dynamics and examine how ballet has historically acted as both a catalyst for progressive change. Department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Africanist Traditions
courses.description: This course examines the history and influence of African American vernacular dance and performance traditions upon American popular, concert, and commercial dance performance, beginning with black-faced minstrelsy and ending with 20th century traditions such as hip hop. It will bring forward and clear retention of Africanist culture rooted deeply in the American Aesthetic, as evidenced in the work of such major choreographers as George Balanchine, Alvin Alley, and others. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Dance Production
courses.description: Students will develop communication and visual skills used to collaborate with the creative and production teams, build production knowledge to aid in the process and create documentation to use in the pre-production, production, and post-production process. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Teaching Methods
courses.description: Students will gain skills for teaching an Introduction to Modern Dance class, articulate goals as teachers, and develop the means to guide students in experiential, analytical, and creative exercises. Through readings, practice, and discussion, students gain information about issues involved in teaching dance to beginning adult students. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Teaching Methods
courses.description: Students will gain skills for teaching an Introduction to Modern Dance class, articulate goals as teachers, and develop the means to guide students in experiential, analytical, and creative exercises. Through readings, practice, and discussion, students gain information about issues involved in teaching dance to beginning adult students. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Choreography, Performance, Production, and Design Lab (CCP&D)
courses.description: This course will provide undergraduate students with the opportunity to work on graduate student projects and obtain additional skills in performance and production. Dance majors only; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Third Year Seminar
courses.description: This course is designed to prepare dance students for post-graduation life with a focus on the field of dance. Students will create a dance reel, personal statement and professional CV. Topic discussions will encompass money management, networking, auditions, creating the dance environment you wish to live in, and finding the "right" place to name a few. Prerequisite: Completion of DANCE 191. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall DANCE 400-499

courses.title: Floorwork III/IV
courses.description: Advanced Floorwork is to scaffold on the industrious technical baseline of our dancing and align it with our risk-taking and choice-making sensibilities through integration of more complex action and sequences. We will continue to build upon the integrity and responsive nature of the feet with real-time challenges that open up and strengthen our ability to adapt to shifting forces/environments. In doing so we will begin to find clearer lines of communication through the joints facilitating ease of movement, passing of force, and quick reaction times. Prerequisite: Completion of DANCE 201. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.description: This course will be an intermediate/advanced modern dance technique class taught by dance faculty and guest artists, offering a variety of styles and trends in the field. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Spring

courses.title: Advanced Partnering
courses.description: Building on established contact improvisational partnering and basic momentum based partnering, this course will scaffold upon that acumen to engage in sophisticated and challenging partner work. Prerequisite: DANCE 207 with a grade of B or better. Dance majors only; department consent required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.description: Dancers will learn repertory by faculty and guest artists, to be performed at the end of the course. Dancers will also design and conduct a residency in a public school setting. Dancers may be cast, by audition, in one work for one credit or two works for two credits. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Spring

courses.title: Dramaturgy for Physical Performance
courses.description: This course exposes students to the field of dramaturgy, a creative and scholarly practice in which individuals assist a choreographer, director, and, in general, a creative team through a variety of research-based practices. To prepare students to engage in dramaturgy, this course surveys relevant literature in the field, including recently published articles and books in dramaturgy, which has exploded in North American research in the last decade, and theoretical texts that offer larger frames to consider the nature of dramaturgy in physical performance, particularly dance. Students also work in developing skills for specific tasks often associated with dramaturgy: leading feedback sessions, creating different formats for assessing a piece's overall structure, developing research packets and questions, and facilitating post-performance discussions, among others. Whenever possible, students enrolled in the course will be attached to ongoing performance projects, so that the course will always be oriented toward making performance and finding ways to enhance an ongoing creative process. Students will be assessed on a series of short written responses, participation in artist's rehearsal, and their ability to design creative research portfolios that include visual, physical, and textual research. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Dance and Technology
courses.description: Collaborations in Media introduces the hybrid fusion (also called Videodance or Dance for the Camera) of movement, camera work and editing on Final Cut Pro. A highly interdisciplinary course that attracts students from Dance, Performing Arts Technology, Art and Design, and Screen Arts and Culture, it challenges students from diverse disciplines to compose short works for the screen in a series of 5-6 assignments. The course hosts an Annual UM Dance on Camera Festival of works curated from that year's New York Dance on Camera Festival at Lincoln Center. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Dance Across Borders
courses.description: This course is an upper division and graduate level seminar that explores diverse dance cultures' global travel and relocation from the lens of dance and transnationalism. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Dancing Women/Dancing Queer
courses.description: This course, which is situated in dance and performance studies, will look at representations of gender, sexuality, and artistry across a variety of sites from ballet to modern dance, from the concert stage to the music video, and from Broadway to avant garde solo performance. Although the primary frames of analysis are gender and sexuality, the course works from the premise that these questions can never be considered separately from questions of race, class, and nationality, among other possible vectors of identity. Too, the course imagines how feminist and queer methods of art making are essential to gender and sexuality studies. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Accompanying Movement
courses.description: In this course, musicians will learn how to accompany for kinesthetic, movement-based art forms through the study and analysis of western dance technique classes. Using both Modern Dance and Ballet Technique courses typically offered in the Department of Dance, musicians will observe and analyze the structure and content of the class, will research the specific genre of the class, and by observing the methods of communication used between instructor and dance student, instructor and musician, and dance student and musician, they will learn how to collaborate in a dance class. Throughout the term, the student will accompany individual combinations so that by the end of the term, they will be able to provide an appropriate standard of music for an entire class session. This will provide the musician with an entry into collaboration with movement-based art forms. Prerequisite: Performance or Composition background with Sophomore standing or higher. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Writing Dancing
courses.description: This course focuses on writers who assess and describe dance from a variety of perspectives, for a variety of audiences, in a variety of formats. Study of major dance critics from the 19th century to the present day will also provide a springboard for students to experiment and the process of writing themselves. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Ballet Pedagogy
courses.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of ballet pedagogy, equipping students with the knowledge and skills to teach ballet effectively to diverse populations. Topics include classical technique, teaching methodologies, musicality, anatomical principles, classroom management, and curriculum development. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Students review their dance training, articulate new goals and begin to develop portfolios to support both artistic and career goals. This will include sessions on grant writing, program planning, marketing, and sessions on archiving of materials and current technology/media used in supporting these aims. Prerequisite: Successful completion of DANCE 391. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Senior Concert
courses.description: Choreography and production of one solo and one group work for presentation in a thesis concert. Prerequisite: DANCE 372. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Senior Concert
courses.description: Choreography and production of one solo and one group work for presentation in a thesis concert. Prerequisite: DANCE 372. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Special Topics
courses.description: A survey of academic and studio-based dance practices not yet offered in the current curriculum. Course instructors may be from resident faculty or guest artists. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Special projects designed by students under faculty supervision. Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring, Summer

courses.title: Field Experience
courses.description: Performance, teaching, and directing of projects for the local community (non-University related). Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring, Summer DANCE 500-599

courses.title: Research in Action (RIA) 1: Research Methods in Dance
courses.description: This course equips students with the knowledge and skills to engage in dance research. It introduces them to the rich material resources of the University and the broader research community. A range of theoretical frameworks and methodologies will be addressed, as will strategies for designing a research project, determining a clear rationale and appropriate parameters, and articulating particular research questions. The aim is for students to understand current debates, the nature of evidence and argument, and the relationships between practice, theory and criticism. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Research in Action (RIA) 2: Approaching Praxis
courses.description: This course helps students consider how dancemaking is an act of theorizing and, to, how reading and writing theory might be a form of feeding one's artistic practice. The aim of the course is to interrogate key questions and issues currently shaping the dance field, and to consider how these questions inform students' practice, especially as they prepare for their summer fieldwork as a step toward their thesis project. Students will engage critically with selected readings, performances, and studio research in order to develop a sophisticated grasp of different approaches to dance-making and scholarship, and greater fluency in working across dance theory-practice areas. Assessment for the course will be by written, oral and embodied assignments - all explicitly shaped to deepen the students' artmaking and performance practices. Prerequisite: DANCE 501 (C or better). Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Research in Action (RIA) 3: Self-Evaluation Report
courses.description: This course requires students to reflect critically on their first year of Master's level study and to write a report. The form the report takes is up to the student, and may be creatively engaged, including alternative formats that might take digital form, a transcript of a "self-interview," or a letter written to an audience of the student’s choice. (3,500 words or equivalent). Detailed reference should be made to the student’s learning across all courses taken in the first year of the program. Not all courses must be discussed in detail, but there should be attention to both breadth and depth of experiences. The aim is for students to demonstrate competence in working across theory-practice realms and to identify realistic next steps and further training needs. The paper is due on August 1 and should be submitted to the Director of Graduate Studies, who will evaluate the paper and submit the grade. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter and Spring

courses.title: Ballet
courses.description: This course focuses on proper alignment, placement, body awareness, self-discovery, self-correction, execution and awareness of other dancers and teaching techniques. The vocabulary encompasses a logical development of more advanced barre and center work including advanced pirouettes, enchainments, and grand allegro. Through repetition of material, students will be challenged to reverse combinations, recite terminology, and demonstrate combinations without the assistance of demonstration by the instructor. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Graduate Physical Practice
courses.description: This course will provide a critical and research-driven approach to physical practice. Distinct from a standard "technique" class, priority is given to experimental approaches to movement generation, individual lineage/training of students, social-cultural influences on movement aesthetics, and pedagogical strategies for communicating movement qualities and textures. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Contemporary Dance
courses.description: This course develops movement skills and concepts within contemporary dance genres towards effective performance. It stresses the development of musicality, versatility, and expressivity, sensitivity, range, control, and clarity of performance, with sound anatomical principles as well as a wide range of spatial, rhythmic and dynamic qualities. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: World Dance
courses.description: This course explores dance forms beyond the traditional Euro-American theatrical genres, including dances of Asia, Africa, the Americas, Caribbean and pacific Rim. The aim of this course is to increase student knowledge of these forms through studio practice, discussion and readings, and to further their understanding of spatial, religious, and social restrictions/conventions. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Ann Arbor Dance Works: Technique
courses.description: This course will be intermediate-advanced modern dance technique class taught by resident dance faculty and guest artists, offering techniques that reflect a variety of styles and trends in the field. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Spring

courses.title: Phrase Work
courses.description: This will be a practice that compels and demands attention to shifting dynamics and form through learning and performing phrases of movement with emphasis on sequence, syntax, rhythmic clarity and elasticity. Gaining fluency through a range of physical skills, participants will employ somatic, creative, and intellectual practices to delve into questions of lineage and ideation. This course is envisioned as a grad only physical practice with the potential for rotating and guest faculty. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Field Experience: Dance Technique
courses.description: This course is designed for students who wish to undertake a dance technique project beyond the University of Michigan. The 'field' of study is determined by the student, as is the nature and scope of the project, in consultation with a designated advisor. Such a project can be undertaken locally, nationally or overseas, with the number of credit hours determined by the project's parameters, timescale and complexity. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring, Summer

courses.title: Independent Study: Dance Technique
courses.description: This course is designed for students who wish to study one or more dance techniques in-depth. The nature of the investigation is student-designed and directed, in consultation with a designated advisor. Both methodology and outcomes can be either practice-based or follow more traditional scholarly forms, for example, a final research paper or conference presentation. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring, Summer

courses.title: University Dance Company (UDC)
courses.description: This course consists of a commitment to the creative and rehearsal process in preparation for performances of new or repertory work for the annual University Production dance performance. The cast of student dancers works with a choreographer to evolve a finished production - involving the integration of choreographic intention and style with musical score, sets, props, costuming, video, or other scenic components. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Movement Research: Reviving 20th-21st Century Dances
courses.description: In this project-based course, students will deepen their knowledge of the modern dance legacy by researching and performing a selection of short dances or choreographic excerpts from the early 20th century to the present. They will inhabit movement vocabularies and performance styles, analyze choreographic structure, investigate the creative process, learn about the production elements of a dance work, and research its cultural and historical context. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Ann Arbor Dance Works Repertory
courses.description: In this course, dancers will learn modern dance repertory taught by resident faculty and guest artists, which will be performed for the public in a formal performance at the end of the course. Dancers will be cast in repertory works by audition. The course will also include a residency in a community setting; the residency may entail the offering of master classes, lecture demonstrations, workshops and performances. Dancers may be cast in one work for 1 credit, or two works for 2 credits. Dancers will assist with designing and implementing community residencies, and will learn how to transfer. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Spring

courses.title: Special Topics: Performance/Repertory
courses.description: Special Topics courses in performance/repertory allow students the flexibility to pursue discipline-specific or interdisciplinary study in-depth, led by a specialist instructor/guest artist. The courses will differ thematically, dependent upon the teaching and research expertise of the instructor. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring, Summer

courses.title: Independent Study: Performance/Repertory
courses.description: This course is designed for students who wish to study one or more dance performance or repertory experiences in-depth. The nature of the investigation is student-designed and directed, in consultation with a designated advisor. Both methodology and outcomes can be either practice-based or follow more traditional scholarly forms, for example, a final research paper or conference presentation. courses.title: Solo Composition and Performance
courses.description: Throughout this course, students will develop a personal practice that stretches their imaginative and intellectual definitions of themselves as performers and creators. Class time will be used as a laboratory to create and analyze multiple approaches to choreography and performance, as well as conceptualize what differences emerge through the process of "making" versus "performing". Students will investigate how the physicality's, habits, and rhythms already in our bodies are shaped culturally, politically, and emotionally. Students develop their own definitions for words commonly associated with choreographic process, such as time, space, form, meaning, energy, representation, and structure. What cultural or aesthetic references live within the language we choose to discuss dance? Short in-class assignments are meant to be experimental and approached with curiosity. Supplemental readings and viewings will contextualize class work in relationship to historical trends in contemporary dance. Each student will propose a final project relevant to their own research that will be performed in an informal showcase at the end of the semester. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Graduate Performance
courses.description: Students enrolled in the course will create new work, likely building on studies begun in coursework elsewhere, through a series of rehearsals across the winter semester, with a performance at the end of the semester in the Department's Theatre. The work may be solo or group work, but must demonstrate command of all elements of theatrical production: creating a rehearsal schedule; communicating with a creative team, including designers and technical staff; conducting technical and dress rehearsals; and performance. Required for first-year MFA Dance students. Second year MFA Dance students have the option of repeating the course, though must contribute work not presented as part of their thesis. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Performance Improvisation 1
courses.description: This course is devoted to in-depth study and practice of improvisation as a performing art In improvisation, insight, inspiration, composition and performance occur simultaneously. The constant flux and exchange of doing and reflecting heightens awareness of compositional choices. The improvising performer works without a net, where every choice and action is visible and audible. Recognizing the three strands of improvisational practice: bodily exploration, honing and cultivating aesthetic values and observational skills, and composing dances in the moment will influence and shape the learning process. Each student will be called upon to develop as an artist, a soloist, and as a collaborator as we build a movement and music ensemble that can co-create shapely, coherent, short and long pieces through improvisation. The course will culminate in a performance at the close of the semester. Two reading and writing assignments per week will support and encourage thoughtful analysis and practice. The final summary paper will connect experience in class, journal entries, discussions and the reading assignments into a meaningful anthology. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Mapping Movement and Place: Site-Specific Performance
courses.description: Through readings, video viewings and performance projects, this course will examine the creative processes for a variety of contemporary site-specific dance performances. Dancers will conduct research about a chosen site, and will choreography and perform in their own site-specific dance project. Emphasis will be placed upon investigating the social and cultural histories of the chosen site, and of its environmental and/or architectural features. Prerequisite: DANCE 531 and 532. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Dramaturgy for Physical Performance
courses.description: This course exposes students to the field of dramaturgy, a creative and scholarly practice in which individuals assist a choreographer, director, and, in general, a creative team through a variety of research-based practices. To prepare students to engage in dramaturgy, this course surveys relevant literature in the field, including recently published articles and books in dramaturgy, which has exploded in North American research in the last decade, and theoretical texts that offer larger frames to consider the nature of dramaturgy in physical performance, particularly dance. Students also work in developing skills for specific tasks often associated with dramaturgy: leading feedback sessions, creating different formats for assessing a piece's overall structure, developing research packets and questions, and facilitating post-performance discussions, among others. Whenever possible, students enrolled in the course will be attached to ongoing performance projects, so that the course will always be oriented toward making performance and finding ways to enhance an ongoing creative process. Students will be assessed on a series of short written responses, participation in artist's rehearsal, and their ability to design creative research portfolios that include visual, physical, and textual research. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required

courses.description: Topics allow student the flexibility to pursue discipline-specific or interdisciplinary study in-depth, led by a specialist instructor/guest artist. courses.title: Screendance and New Media 1
courses.description: This course examines the creative potential of integrating choreography and technology through projects in experimental video, social media and the internet, interactive performance, improvisation, and sound design. Supplemental screenings and readings will provide historical and theoretical context to inspire new possibilities for pursuing mediated choreographic practices. We will broadly consider the term "choreography" to research the ways in which bodies and information move through time and space via a multitude of technological interferences. We will discuss what becomes identified as "technology" and the social, political, and ecological consequences of engaging with these systems. Critical attention will be given to the relationship between technology and visibility, specifically in regards to race, gender, sexuality, class, and ability. Through what labor do technological systems come into the world and who benefits from their being here? Each student will write a treatment for a final project of their own design which can take shape in a variety of forms: video, essay, live performance, etc. As a class, we will organize a public event to share final projects with the community. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Screendance and New Media Portfolio
courses.description: Students will compile their portfolio by creating an appropriate range of screendance works, the number and duration of which will be determined in consultation with their Portfolio Advisor. They may choose solo and/or group works, and edit their material using non-linear video editing software. The Screendance Portfolio will be accompanied by a written proposal. Prerequisite: DANCE 542. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Dancing Women/Dancing Queer
courses.description: This course, which is situated in dance and performance studies, will look at representations of gender, sexuality, and artistry across a variety of sites from ballet to modern dance, from the concert stage to the music video, and from Broadway to avant garde solo performance. Although the primary frames of analysis are gender and sexuality, the course works from the premise that these questions can never be considered separately from questions of race, class, and nationality, among other possible vectors of identity. Too, the course imagines how feminist and queer methods of art making are essential to gender and sexuality studies. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.description: This course introduces students to the scientific principles underlying the complexities of dance movement. Utilizing visual stimuli, touch, writing and drawing, readings, and experiential modalities such as Ideokinesis, Feldenkrais, visualization, and Alexander technique, students will learn to apply the principles of anatomy and kinesiology, as they pertain to dance. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.description: This course focuses on writers who assess and describe dance from a variety of perspectives, for a variety of audiences, in a variety of formats. Study of major dance critics from the 19th century to the present day will also provide a springboard for students to experiment with the process of writing themselves. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Black Dance Performance: From Ritual to the Stage
courses.description: Using a chronological and geographical approach, this course examines Africanist performance trends in dance music and theater, tracing them from West Africa through the African Diaspora in the Americas. Movement and aesthetic commonalities of these forms will be studied, together with the socio-culture conditions that contributed to their creation and which continue to influence American dance and culture today. Issues of identity, ethnicity and stereotyping through the idiom of African-Americans vernacular and concert dance will also be addressed. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: George Balanchine and the Transformation of American Dance
courses.description: This seminar examines the life and works of dancer/choreographer George Balanchine and his influence on 20th-21st century dance. Balanchine's fusion of "fine" and "popular" art resulted in a new American style of classical dance as well as a reinvigoration of dance forms in American musical theater and films. He has been compared to Shakespeare in the depth and scope of his work and ranked with Picasso and Stravinsky as one of the titans of twentieth century arts. Born in Tsarist Russia, Balanchine survived the 1917 Revolution to make a career in America (1933-83). He absorbed influences from nineteenth century Franco-Russian classical ballet at the Russian Imperial Ballet where he was trained and danced in the Tchaikovsky ballets. He participated in the artistic ferment surrounding the Russian revolution and in the modernist innovations of Diaghilev's Ballets Russes collaborating with Matisse, Stravinsky and Prokofiev. He changed the face of American dance by founding a new kind of modern American ballet company, The New York City Ballet, creating innovative dances for a new kind of American classical dancer (including the first native American ballerina, Maria Tallchief and the African American dancer, Arthur Mitchell). As a teacher, he transformed American ballet technique. But Balanchine was also a vital part of American popular culture, working in Broadway musical theater and Hollywood films. His work with African-American dancers Katherine Dunham, The Nicholas Brothers, and Josephine Baker influenced their development and his own. This course complements and supplements the more general topic and broadly themed courses in the curriculum with an opportunity for students to focus in on an extensive and intensive examination of a key figure in the history of dance and his works. Students will gain experience in original historical research with archival material, concentrating on primary sources of all kinds in conjunction with intensive analysis of Balanchine’s choreography. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Pedagogy: Practices and Principles
courses.description: This course offers an overview to pedagogical methods in dance: technique/physical practice; composition; community engagement; diversity, equity, and inclusion; theory; history; and media. The course is usually taught by the Director of Graduate Studies, who will facilitate guest lectures from the entire dance faculty. Students will be evaluated on a series of short assignments related to the various methods offered, and the final course assignment will be a cumulative teaching portfolio, including revisions of materials such as a teaching philosophy, syllabi, and assignments. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Pedagogy Dance Technique
courses.description: Exploration of theoretical concepts, principles, and methods of pedagogical trends through lectures, readings, videos, discussion and teaching practicum with the goal of developing a sound basis for continued growth and effectiveness as dance educators. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Pedagogy Dance Composition
courses.description: This course addresses strategies for teaching undergraduate-level Dance Composition. Graduate students will participate in teaching a sophomore-level majors course, 232 Dance Composition IV: Mapping Movement and Sound. They will lead improvisational exercises and provide critical feedback sessions for students. They will also research the use of music/sound in the works of selected choreographers and present this research. They will be assessed through these and other assignments, including self-evaluation papers, teaching philosophy statements, and the creation of a syllabus for beginning-level dance composition students. Graduate Dance majors only; instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Pedagogy Dance History
