courses.title: Introduction to Acting I
courses.description: Basic principles of acting for non-performance majors. The class introduces the fundamentals of acting to help the student “discover” him/herself through improvisation and other exercises. Grounds the student in basic acting theory. Instructor permission required; primarily for non-majors; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Acting II
courses.description: Continuation of 101 with attention to scene study. Instructs how to analyze and approach the written text and embody character. Instructor permission required; primarily for non-majors; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Acting for the Camera
courses.description: Introduces students to the basic techniques of acting for the camera through the use of video. Sound foundation acting principles will be presented with an emphasis on exercise, scene and monologue work, and closing with scene orchestration via a basic two-camera with switcher recording, utilizing a mix of selected dramatic material and/or existing film scripts. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 101 or instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Stage Make-up
courses.description: Covers the foundations of stage make-up; basic corrective, manipulating the features with the highlight and shadows and old age make-up applications, script analysis for make-up and an introduction to prosthetics and wig care. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Movement I
courses.description: Aims to provide performers with a working knowledge of their bodies. Exercises, improvisation, and other techniques will aid in developing awareness of the body as an expressive medium. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Acting I: Ensemble and Imagination
courses.description: Introduction to acting with emphasis on freeing and expanding an actor's imagination, exploration of the psycho-physical connection, and ensemble building. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Acting II: Observation and Action
courses.description: Exploration of expanding the actor's sensory capacity, and subsequently honing that capacity to in-the-moment responses to scene partner, and the introduction of the objective-action approach. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 181 and instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Voice I
courses.description: Course designed to help the would-be performer begin to discover and develop the vocal instrument. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Introduction to Drama and Theatre
courses.description: Introduces the student to as many basic elements of the theatre, practical and theoretical, as time allows. It also presents a number of key plays from various periods, and examines them from the point of view of their dramatic qualities, theatrical strengths, social and political contexts, their performance history, and their relevance today. This course is geared toward students who do not have extensive experience attending or participating in the theatre. Theatre and Musical Theatre majors may only elect to take this course in their first semester. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Global Theatre and Ethnic Studies
courses.description: Surveys performance histories of diverse cultural communities of the United States. Students study transnational origins and cultural contexts for multi-cultural theatre: African American (African, Caribbean, Afro-Latino), Native American, Latin American, Asian American (Southeast Asian, East Asian), Middle Eastern, and others. Students study multi-cultural literatures and practices in the United States. Students learn about performance histories and practices of culturally diverse communities in the United States, study performance aesthetics emerging from Asian American, African American, Latin American and Native American communities, and learn how to read and analyze diverse plays by United States authors in cultural context. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Introductory Playwriting
courses.description: A creative writing course in the rudiments of playwriting, with special attention to the one-act play. Students are accepted on the basis of a portfolio. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Modern Rituals/Traditional Practices
courses.description: Trains students in performance techniques grounded in various cultural traditions: choral singing, masking, poetry, vocal call and responses, dance, martial arts, and mimicry. Embodied studio practice emphasizes aesthetics of diverse cultural communities. Guest artists and instructors interact with students in the instructional space. Students learn how practice emerges from culturally specific contexts, how to embody culturally specific aesthetics and practices, and they train in the vocal, physical and theatrical expression skills. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Research Methodology for Design and Production
courses.description: The course examines best practices for locating, organizing, and synthesizing research materials in the development of theatrical production creative processes. students will discover and utilize a broad range of research methods, identify primary sources, and create a digital library for future projects and productions. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Design
courses.description: This course introduces students to the process of designing scenery, costumes and lighting for the stage. It deals both with finding and developing ideas and with finding ways to express them. It provides students with a process with which to approach to play and begin to design, as well as starting to develop a theatrical vocabulary which will serve as a foundation for future design work. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Directing I
courses.description: The history of directors, function and responsibilities of a director, relationships with designers, playwrights, stage managers, technical/artisan staff, actors, dramaturgs. Identifying styles of theatre, stage types, floor plans. Also covers script interpretation/analysis, director’s research, resources, directorial concepts, conceptualization of a play, interpretation. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Introduction to Stage Management
courses.description: Principles and practices of stage management, including rehearsal coordination, prompt book preparation, and director/cast/crew relationships during rehearsal for theatre, opera, and musical theatre. Combines classroom instruction with practicum experience. Students assistant-stage-manage a University Productions show during the semester; participate in rehearsals and performances. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Technical Theatre Practices
courses.description: Introduction to the basic principles and practices of stagecraft: scenic materials, construction, painting, stage lighting, and costuming. Lectures and lab (shop assignment for a mainstage production). Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Production Practicum I
courses.description: Laboratory in theatre production. Students work in stagecraft, scenic painting, lighting, props, costuming for mainstage productions. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Production Practicum II
courses.description: Second-level laboratory in theatre production. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 251 and instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Lighting Design I
courses.description: Introduction to the components of stage lighting, including an in-depth exploration of the functions and controllable properties of stage lighting. Topics include color theory, optics, electricity, distribution, and equipment. Industry standards regarding control systems, organizational standards, and collaborative techniques will also be covered. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Scene Design I
courses.description: This is a beginning course in scenic design with an emphasis on text analysis. Expression of the production concept, style and period is studied by use of the elements of design. This includes analyzing and discussing plays as the inspiration for a design, some history of design, considering the three-dimensional world of a stage, and how to make basic drawings and models for a stage design. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Production Practicum III
courses.description: Exploration of principles of theatre crafts and practices under faculty supervision. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Production Practicum IV
courses.description: Exploration of principles of theatre crafts and practices under faculty supervision. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Design Rendering
courses.description: Study in the techniques, materials and theory of communicating the costume and scenic design idea. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Costume Construction
courses.description: Investigates the basic hand and machine sewing techniques and skills in the construction of theatrical costumes. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Costume Design I
courses.description: Familiarizes students with art and process of costume design, with strong emphasis on text and character analysis and methods of research. Introduction to basic drawing skills and other visual options in presenting design ideas. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 240 and 277 or instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Movement II
courses.description: Expands the student’s individual range of motion, flexibility, coordination, rhythm, movement vocabulary, physicality and somatic knowledge. Helps the student to build group awareness, stage presence, and introduces basic principles of efficiency of movement, improvisation, partnering, and contact improvisation. Prerequisite: Theatre 172 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Movement III
courses.description: Continuation of Movement II. Focuses on exploring the relations between text, props, human interactions and physicality. Exercises and discussions will revolve around increased subtlety, strength, flexibility, musicality, and dynamics with the goal of heightening the communicative range of the moving body. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 172 and 271 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Stage Combat I
courses.description: Focuses on enabling the actor to extend range of truth and responsibility; imparts a philosophical and historical overview relative to three areas of concentration: unarmed combat, quarterstaff, and single rapier and rapier-and-dagger. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 172 and 181 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: History of Western Silhouettes
courses.description: An examination of clothing silhouettes and prominent designers that have contributed to the narrative of Western dress and fashion. Use of illustrated lectures, critical thinking and writing, and hands-on projects will encourage the student to see the connections between cultural trends and ever evolving silhouettes of fashion and costume design.

courses.title: Acting III: Stakes and Public Argument
courses.description: Further study of objective/action work with emphasis on high stakes, rhetorical skills for argumentation and persuasion, and orienting performance towards its public function; Greek Tragedy and other dramatic sources utilized. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 182 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Acting IV: Heightened Language and Text
courses.description: Exploration of heightened language and text, speaking verse and analyzing verse structure through scansion, identification of antithesis in language and dramatic structure, and continuation of objectve/action work; Shakespeare's texts and other sources utilized. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 281 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Script Analysis
courses.description: This course establishes a comprehensive knowledge of general terms and tools of play analysis. Various ways and trends of analyzing scripts for stage will be studied. Students will read, discuss and write about plays and the various symbols that sustain their messages. Ambiguities and aspects of plot will be explored. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Introduction to Puppetry
courses.description: This course will explore the fundamentals of puppetry, a performance mode that spans the globe and the centuries. There will be hands-on workshops developing and creating several styles of puppets, and students will research puppetry in world performance. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Voice II
courses.description: Expands the understanding and awareness of the basic vocal philosophy and vocabulary established in Voice I, while developing a clearer connection to the demands of text. Continuation of Linklater work, Lessac and Berry study, Skinner speech work, including IPA. Includes poetic text, sonnets and monologues. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 192 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Voice III
courses.description: Expands and refines the student’s individual flexibility, range, and sensitivity to experiencing voice while stimulating vocal imagination. Improvisation and Roy Hart techniques are explored. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 291 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Acting Practicum
courses.description: Instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Voiceover Acting
courses.description: This class focuses on the craft and business of Voice Acting. It is designed to give the actor experience behind the microphone and exposure to the tools and techniques in the highly specialized craft of voice-over work for radio, television, industrial narration, animation, web work, and audio books. Script analysis, character analysis and vocal techniques are explored for single-voiced and multiple-voiced copy. Class time is spent learning about casting and talent agents, promoting and marketing, the audition process, studio etiquette, demos, and the changing world of voiceover technology. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: History of Theatre I
courses.description: The history of theatre from Greeks to Shakespeare, reading selected plays and tracing the history of theatre into dramatic texts generated at particular times and places. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: History of Theatre II
courses.description: The history of theatre from Western Europe and the U.S. from the end of the 17th century to present, focusing on the production of theatre in its historical, social and ideological contexts. Class studies representative plays. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: American Theatre and Drama
courses.description: The study of the American heritage as theatre artists and what has influenced us; principal American dramatists and principal events and issues in the American theatre, mainly in the 20th century. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Global Community Practicum
courses.description: Engages students in research and development of performance projects at a local, community organization or at an international site. The class participates in fieldwork experiences and each individual submits a final project report or thesis at the end of their fieldwork. The Capstone course is collaborative and interdisciplinary and multiple faculty members can supervise and approve student work. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 222 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Contemporary American Theatre and Drama
courses.description: Examines works and developments in American theatre and drama from the past twenty years, especially the diverse and multicultural drama of this period. Looks at elements of class and ethnicity, urbanization, family and community, war and technology, commercialism and consumerism, gender, race, and sexuality. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Intercultural Drama
courses.description: Examines how international dramatic literature in translation comments on global lives and lifestyles. Class reads, analyzes and discusses intercultural plays in cultural context. Written assignments and in-class presentations investigate the political, social, ad cultural impact meaning of intercultural dramatic works. Students learn to analyze themes, structures, characters, and language of intercultural/international plays through the lens of cultural studies. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Intermediate Playwriting
courses.description: Students write the first act of a full-length play. They read from their plays in class and the work is discussed. They also read plays, see performances, keep a journal. At the end of the semester, students give a staged reading of their work for an informal audience. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 227. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Performing Archives and Oral Histories
courses.description: Students use ethnographic or archival sources to create new performance works. Building on histories introduced in 222, they create individual or small group projects. Interpretative text and character work helps to improve individual student performance skills. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 233 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: The Atonement Project
courses.description: This course will teach students about restorative justice, reconciliation, and atonement. We will explore questions of why and how artistic activity can begin and/or support processes of reconciliation for people who have committed crimes and for crime victims. Students in this class will facilitate weekly arts workshops in adult prisons and community venues where former prisoners, crime victims, and the families of those groups can gather together. Focusing on the themes of acknowledgement, apology, and atonement, the workshops will produce original performances, creative writing, and visual art presented at the end of the semester by both the student facilitators and the members of the workshop. Students and workshop participants who give their consent can contribute their work to the Atonement Project website — an online forum designed by the MIT Media Lab — as a means of starting conversations about atonement with web users. Ultimately this course seeks to identify the best strategies for using the arts to address crime and those most affected by it. Fulfills the Race and Ethnicity requirement for SMTD majors only; dual degree students should take an approved course under LSA. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Theatre & Incarceration
courses.description: Artistic practice in prisons has occurred since the inception of prisons themselves, though popular thought tends not to connect the idea of the arts with that of criminal justice systems. This course surveys the history of performance in prisons through the examination of plays written by and about prisoners as well as narratives which chronicle the process of creating theatre in prisons. The course also interrogates various strategies for creating performances in prisons, questioning the utility and goals of each process of creation and seeking to identify those which are most sustainable and which best serve participants in the process. Students will use some of these strategies in practice as they facilitate their workshops in prisons and juvenile detention centers. Fulfills the Race and Ethnicity requirement for SMTD majors only; dual degree students should take an approved course under LSA. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Latina/o Theatre for Social Change
courses.description: This course follows the history of U.S. Latina/o and Latin American paradigms of using theatre for social change. Students in this class will learn about Augusto Boal's Theatre of the Oppressed, the actos of the Chicana/o Movement, guerilla theatre in forms used throughout Latin America, and activist U.S. Latina/o plays. Fulfills the Race and Ethnicity requirement for SMTD majors only; dual degree students should take an approved course under LSA.

courses.title: Disability Theatre
courses.description: This course introduces students to disability theatre, with a particular emphasis on disabled theatre artists’ creative innovations. In addition to providing a historical and theoretical overview of key artists events, and performances, the class also equips students to incorporate accessibility best practices into their own work.

courses.title: Mental Health and the Broadway Musical
courses.description: The course examines the role of musical theatre in mediating mental health. Through analysis of eight broadway musicals, students will learn to identify shifts in psychiatric theory and its representation through theatrical devices, all while developing tools for responsibly engaging mental health in their own work.

courses.title: Devising Theatre
courses.description: The course is a laboratory course for play development. The class creates collaborative theatrical works from text, visual art, movement, stories and/or contemporary events. The class develops performance through improvisation, then organizes and evaluates their work using principles of dramatic structure, and play analysis. Dramaturgy and directing skills are introduced through studio practice and critique. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Directing III
courses.description: Covers period styles from Greek to avant garde, styles of performance (realism, naturalism, expressionism, absurdist, farce, experimental). Explore contemporizing of a play. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 242 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Stage Management Practicum: Plays
courses.description: Methods of stage management, including rehearsal coordination, prompt book preparation, and director/cast/crew relationships during rehearsal period, for plays. Students are assigned as stage managers for Theatre productions. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 351 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Scenic Construction I
courses.description: For the beginning design and technical student, focusing on in-depth study of scenic construction and materials used in construction. Topics: drafting of construction drawings; developing of working drawings; basic electricity; working with wood, foams, fabric, plastics, and metals; hardware used in construction/rigging. Requires working in shop, load-in and strike of a production. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250 and 362 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Production Practicum V
courses.description: Exploration of principles of theatre crafts and practices under faculty supervision. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter THTREMUS 352: Production Practicum VI (1–3 credit hours) Exploration of principles of theatre crafts and practices under faculty supervision. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Sound for the Theatre
courses.description: Principles and practices of sound for the theatre; potential which sound can bring to a theatre production; actual sound projects. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Lighting Design II
courses.description: An in-depth exploration into the development and execution of a lighting design, and the lighting potentials of a wide variety of facilities, production styles, and lighting equipment. Includes work on the development of communication skills with directors and shops via value sketches and lighting plots. Prerequisite: Theatre 256 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Scene Design II
courses.description: Some advanced model-making and drawing skills; the process of conceptualizing and articulating design ideas. Exploration of the unique characteristics of proscenium, arean, and thrust staging. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 260 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Costume Design II
courses.description: This is an advanced course in which students will explore and practice the process of costume design. Course work will consist of a series of projects using specific texts further developing skills in text analysis, research, drawing and painting as related to the art of costume design. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 270 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Physical Theatre
courses.description: Exposes the actor to the dynamics of gesture, the physical foundations of character and interaction, the architecture of stage space and the creation of original work. Based on work of Jacques Lecoq, techniques include commedia, chorus, dance, mime, neutralist, and clown. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: Stage Combat II
courses.description: Continuation of Stage Combat I, leading to SAFD certification. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 192, 274, 282, and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Acting V: Subtext and Irony
courses.description: Scene study with emphasis on exploring subtext, irony, contradiction, complex social dynamics, and a dialectical approach to objectives (will and counter-will) and characterization; the plays of Anton Chekhov and other sources utilized. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 282 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Acting VI: 20th & 21st Century American Realism
courses.description: Examines modern and contemporary American playwrights and their works through scene study. Students study the theory and technique of Constantin Stanislavski as realized by the Group Theater of the early 20th century. Students will study monologues and scenes taken from the American Theater to cultivate skill in exploring text through action and achieving emotional truthfulness in performance. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 381 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: On Camera I
courses.description: Exploration of the fundamentals of acting techniques as they relate to the medium; concentration on purposeful relaxation, image work, subtext, and reemphasis on basic action playing. Methods include improvisation, story telling, monologues, and scenes. Subject matter will be of a contemporary nature and will utilize in-class critique. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 282 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Performing Arts Management
courses.description: An overall look at the administrative aspects of the performing arts, using a Theatre company as the standard model, but with a look at orchestras, dance, and opera. Exploration of theatre development, profit vs. non-profit companies, role of board of directors, unions, budgeting, marketing, public relations, and fundraising. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Practicum in Performing Arts Management
courses.description: Practical work in the management of the performing arts, principally theatre, through assisting in the creation of live performing arts presentations. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter THTREMUS 387, 388: Studio I, II (2 credits) The ongoing work each semester includes scene work, monologues, auditions, readings, and occasional short plays; provides opportunity to expand roles and styles of performance. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Stage Dialects
courses.description: Introduces students to specific methods for acquiring stage dialects. Work includes International Phonetic alphabet and Standard American Speech/Dialect. Students listen to and perform scenes and monologues in each dialect, which may include Standard American, Standard British, Cockney, Irish, American Southern, French, South African, and Spanish. Prerequisite: Theatre 192 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Topics in Drama
courses.description: Covers specialized topics in theatre and drama, which vary from semester to semester. The purpose is to explore in depth aspects of theatre that cannot be covered in existing courses, such as a play or special subject. Typically offered Fall, Winter, Spring

courses.title: Directed Reading
courses.description: Special reading project under faculty supervision. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Allows special work in directing, design, theatre studies, or other specialized areas. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter THTREMUS 403, 404: Design & Production Seminar I, II (1 credit) Active discussion courses which explore issues of contemporary theatre, particularly in relation to design and production. These courses broaden the student’s knowledge of contemporary theatre artists and practices, and sharpens esthetic judgment of productions. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter THTREMUS 410: Creating Original Theatre (3 credit hours) The main thrust of this course is to examine different techniques for, modes of, and approaches to creating what is commonly called "theatre" and perhaps more generally now "performance." Each student will be expected and encouraged to break the perceived established rules associated with making theatre while creating their new whatever-it-takes-to-make-the-idea-understood styles with their own sets of rules. We will use whatever it takes: sound recorded or live, objects, paint, puppets, actors, projection, costume, make-up, set, light as appropriate and possible. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Fundraising and the Arts
courses.description: A review and analysis of philanthropy and development in America’s cultural life, and the role of both the public and private sectors. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Advanced Playwriting
courses.description: Students write a dramatic text, complete a series of assigned technique exercises and material reading, participate in class discussions and live readings. Instructor permission required; typically offered as needed

courses.title: Playwriting Toward Production
courses.description: Student must have written an original play. Class is a collaboration between student designers, actors, producers, and playwrights; analyzes the evolution of a script from its writing to its production. Students rewrite and workshop their plays and present them before an audience at the end of the semester. Instructor permission required; students must have written a script; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Producing in the American Theatre
courses.description: A history of American theatre emphasizing the development of producing techniques coupled with significant productions in the American theatre of the 20th Century. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 385, 386, and Junior or Senior standing. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Theatre Pedagogy
courses.description: This course explores teaching drama in the secondary school, teaching theatre in higher education, and using drama-in-education techniques in all levels of teaching. The course explores ways to approach theatre in teaching and learning that promotes a student-centered, curiosity-driven environment and takes into account a variety of cognitive and learning styles.

courses.title: Legal Issues in the Theatre
courses.description: Theatre’s collective bargaining fundaments/issues. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 435. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: African American Drama
courses.description: Spanish philosopher and novelist George Santayana wrote, “Those who cannot remember their past are condemned to repeat their mistakes.” Our national social and political climate is summoning us to look beyond the spectacles and the narratives that keep us from change. This course focuses on the foundations of (Black) African American Theater by asking: Who defines and controls the narrative, the aesthetics? Who tells the story? Does the narrative matter? More importantly, for whom does (Black) African American Theater speak? Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Directing Project
courses.description: Students continue their preparation for a professional career or graduate studies in directing by directing a studio play. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 441 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Directing Colloquium I
courses.description: Senior directing students meet to discuss final projects, do presentations of concept of their play, design and casting choices, practical realization of the play, choice of script, and post-production discussions/reviews. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 442 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Stage Management for Operas and Musicals
courses.description: Seminar portion covers methods of stage management including rehearsal coordination, prompt book or musical score preparation, record keeping, and director, conductor / orchestra, cast and crew relationships during the rehearsal period.; students are also assigned as stage managers for School of Music, Theatre & Dance opera or musical theatre productions. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 245, 351, and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Advanced Stage Management
courses.description: Further study of the principles and practices of stage management including personnel management, problem solving, range of work environments and contracts, union rules, and touring. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 245 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Production Practicum VII
courses.description: An introduction to production and management skills needed by the technical director: drafting of construction drawings, cost analysis of materials, metal and wood fabrication, environmental/structural safety, scenery rigging, movement, mechanization. Students work on studio projects and department productions. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 352 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Period Costume Techniques
courses.description: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to apply construction techniques for historical structures that reshape the body and change a person's proportions required for theatrical costuming. Students will explore fabric manipulation, historical detail creation and understructures used in creating wearable costumes for the stage. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Lighting Design III
courses.description: Advanced study of lighting design, incorporating increasingly difficult texts, facilities, and production styles; alternative venues and production styles. Includes several major projects. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 356. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Scene Design III
courses.description: For students whose main interest is scenic design. Hones the conceptual process and develops deeper awareness of style as related to text. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 360. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Production Practicum VIII
courses.description: Advanced level production practicum under faculty supervision. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 451 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Drafting
courses.description: A study of the principles of scenery drafting; basic skills of geometric construction; steps for making production drawings. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Scene Painting for the Theatre
courses.description: A study of the methods and materials of painting scenery for stage productions; characteristics of various scene painting materials; lab work devoted to color, perspective, utilization of various materials. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 250. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: History of Decor
courses.description: This course is a chronological study of the decorative styles of interiors and exteriors in Western architecture and their applications to the stage. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: History of Theatre Architecture and Stage Design
courses.description: This course covers the origins and evolution of the theatre building and theatrical design and technology with the corresponding political, social, and artistic context. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Costume Design III
courses.description: This is an advanced course in which students will explore and practice the process of costume design. Course work will consist of series of projects using specific texts further developing skills in text analysis, research, drawing, and painting as related to the art of costume design. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 370 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Women’s Pattern Drafting
courses.description: This course introduces the students to the principles and skills of draping, drafting and pattern making techniques utilized in theatrical costume development. Instructor permission required. Typically offered Fall as needed

courses.title: Stage Make-Up
courses.description: Fundamentals of make-up for theatre; study of facial structure, physiology of age, character, and psychology of color. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Tailoring
courses.description: The course introduces the student to the advanced skills of drafting, patterning, and hand construction required in the art of tailoring. Throughout the semester, students learn and refine the components that comprise tailoring techniques for a tailored suit jacket.

courses.title: Theatre and Drama International Study
courses.description: In this global field experience, students will live and study abroad as a part of a supplementary enrichment based on a prior departmental course (prerequisite is determined by the faculty leader). Students will participate in engaged learning opportunities such as research, creative activities, and community engagement. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Topics in Costume Technology
courses.description: Specific topics in one or more of the arts and crafts necessary to costume technology. Areas to be chosen from include: fabric dyeing and painting, millinery, wig design and construction, latex prosthetic, and decorative accessories for the stage. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Fashion and Costume: Global Adornment and Attire
courses.description: This course encourages the student to think critically about connections between the global history of clothing and the complexities of race and ethnicity in cultural contexts, while fostering an appreciation for the interconnected nature of the diversity in adornment and dress. Topics that connect global fashion and adornment will be considered with an emphasis on exposure to quintessential historical or traditional dress of countries and their relation to the global fashion industry. Fulfills the Race and Ethnicity requirement for SMTD majors only; dual degree students should take an approved course under LSA. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Topics in Theatre Technology
courses.description: This course will offer specific topics in one of more of the arts and crafts necessary in theatre technology bridging instructional needs prior to working on realized productions. Topics to include: rigging, mold making, circuiting, automation, soft goods, LX programming, metal work, etc.

courses.title: Acting VII: Contemporary Performance
courses.description: Scene study for further development and utilization of principles learned in Acting I-V, with emphasis on the 20th and 21st century plays. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 381 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Acting VIII: Showcase and Professional Preparation
courses.description: Preparation for professional networking, organizing, and marketing required in the film, television, and theatre industries. Showcase materials prepared to be presented to industry professionals in New York and Los Angeles, with an additional filmed component. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 481 and instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Comedy and Style
courses.description: This course focuses on the principles of performing various comic styles, and may include the work of Moliere, Wilde, Coward, and contemporary playwrights. Advanced scene work will utilize objective-action work, but also consider the actor as communicator to audience. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall

courses.title: On Camera II
courses.description: Concentration on practical techniques to use in selected on-camera situations. Utilization of adjustments needed for compelling, truthful working using various audition and recording formats. Single and multiple camera studio work will be employed. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 483 or instructor permission required. Typically offered Winter THTREMUS 487, 488: Studio III, IV (2 credits) Ongoing work each semester includes scene work, monologues, auditions, readings, and occasional short plays; provides opportunity to expand roles and styles of performance. Prerequisite: THTREMUS 387 and 388; THTREMUS 487 is a prerequisite for THTREMUS 488. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Über Practicum
courses.description: This advanced theatre practicum requires a significant production contribution from the student, such as a major design assignment, stage management, or technical direction. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: American Theatre and Drama

courses.title: Basic Lyric Diction
courses.description: A survey of English, Italian, German, and French Lyric Diction. Basic rules of stage pronunciation for singers are introduced, along with the international phonetic alphabet. Readings with presentations are complemented with class spoken, written, and sung exercises, as well as monthly student performances. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Basic Italian Diction
courses.description: Introduction to singing in Italian according to the principles of the Italian lyric stage. Singing in Latin is briefly introduced. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Basic German Diction
courses.description: German diction according to codified rules of German stage pronunciation. Coaching of repertoire takes place throughout the course. Also includes introduction to singing in English according to common practice, as well as the International Phonetic Alphabet. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Basic French Diction
courses.description: Introduction to singing in French according to common practice. Coaching of repertoire (art songs and operas) takes place throughout the course. Typically offered Fall

courses.title: Introduction to Art Song
courses.description: This course explores the connection between words and music, poet and composer, and singer and pianist through a study of art song and its performance. Through guided listening to historic performances, the class will discover vocal and pianistic styles, repertoire, and performance traditions of art song. In-class discussions will tour the world each week, encountering art song in Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Russia, Britain, and other countries, including America. Typically offered Winter

courses.title: Vocal Literature of Black American Composers
courses.description: Surveys the art songs of African Americans from the beginning of the 20th century to the present. The course includes numerous unpublished works and the analysis of the texts as well as rhythmic, harmonic, and melodic features. Fulfills the Race and Ethnicity requirement for SMTD majors only; dual degree students should take an approved course under LSA. Junior standing or higher; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Czech Vocal Literature
courses.description: This class is a performance class for singers and pianists, presenting an overview of Czech art song and opera. The class will culminate with a public performance. Pre-requisites: Permission of the instructor, facility singing in Italian and German. Instructor Permission Required; offered every other Winter semester

courses.title: Repertoire Preparation
courses.description: Exploration of language, diction, musical style, and interpretation are addressed in weekly sessions with voice students. Work may include: role, audition, and recital preparation. Instructor permission required; typically offered Fall, Winter

courses.title: Chamber Music for Voice and Instruments
courses.description: Designed for singers and instrumentalists to explore chamber music involving voice(s) from the Renaissance to the 21st Century. Ensembles can include all voice types, orchestral instrumentalists, Harpsichord, Piano, Organ, Guitar, and Percussion. Instructor permission required; typically offered Winter

courses.title: Wellness for the Performing Artist
courses.description: This class introduces students to wellness topics such as performance anxiety, stress management, Yoga, reducing injury risk, and Alexander Technique, with the aim exploring the intersection of physical movement, mental health, and performance. Typically offered Fall, Winter.

courses.title: Alexander Technique Intro
courses.description: The goal in this class is to restore the ease and enjoyment of performing by examining habits of tension that can interfere with fluid movement and expanded creativity. Using the self-awareness principles embodied in the Alexander Technique, students learn to restore free and easy breath, let go of unnecessary tension, and reduce self-defeating thoughts that interfere with instinctual freedom. Group and individual instruction provided. Typically offered Fall, Winter. WELLNESS 412/512, Sections 001 & 002 - In-person, Section 003 - Asynchronous: Yoga for Performers (1 credit) This course will consist of the practice and study of Yoga, including postures, breathing, meditation, and philosophy, focusing on the needs of students and performers. We will explore different aspects of the practice and break it down into useful, practical tools. Typically offered Fall, Winter.
